title: std::vector and algorithms: a grade book
summary: Store any number of values in a std::vector, process them with loops and standard algorithms (accumulate, sort, count_if), and meet your first lambda.

steps.title: A list that grows
hints: `std::vector<int> scores;` then inside a `while (std::cin >> score)` loop: `scores.push_back(score);`
Print with a range-based for: `for (int s : scores) std::cout << ' ' << s;`

steps.title: Average, with an algorithm
hints: `std::accumulate(scores.begin(), scores.end(), 0.0)` — the `0.0` (a double) makes the sum a double. With `0` it would be an int.

steps.title: Median: sorting a copy
hints: `std::sort(scores.begin(), scores.end());` sorts the vector in place — fine, because `median` received its own copy.
With `n` sorted values and `mid = n / 2`: odd `n` → `scores[mid]`; even `n` → `(scores[mid - 1] + scores[mid]) / 2.0`.

steps.title: Why does median take a copy?

quiz.question: `average` takes `const std::vector<int>&` but `median` takes `std::vector<int>` (by value). Why is that the right choice for median?
options: It's a mistake — everything should be passed by const reference.
median needs to sort the values. Taking a copy lets it sort freely without changing the caller's vector — and it needs a copy anyway, so taking one by value costs nothing extra.
Vectors can't be sorted through a reference.
Passing by value is faster for vectors.
explanations: `const&` is the right default for read-only access. But median *modifies* the data (it sorts), so const& won't work — and plain `&` would scramble the caller's data.

Exactly. Rule of thumb: read-only → `const T&`; need your own copy anyway → `T` by value; need to change the caller's object → `T&`. The test `median_does_not_reorder_the_callers_scores` checks this contract.
They can — through a non-const reference. But then the caller's vector would be re-ordered, which would surprise them.
Copying a vector copies every element: it's slower, not faster. Here we accept the cost because sorting needs a copy we can modify.

checks.label: Hidden tests for letter_grades and count_at_least pass

hints: letter_grades: loop over the scores, `push_back` a letter chosen with an `if / else if` chain. Check the highest grade first.
count_at_least with an algorithm: `std::count_if(scores.begin(), scores.end(), [threshold](int s) { return s >= threshold; })` returns a count — convert it with `static_cast<int>`.
In main, check `scores.empty()` before calling average/median, which throw on empty input.
